sources.title: Brio (company) - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: # Brio (company). * Edit&action=edit "Edit this page [e]"). **Brio** (stylized **BRIO**) is a wooden toy company founded in Sweden. The company was founded in the small town of Boalt, Scania, Götaland in 1884 by basket maker Ivar Bengtsson. For a long time the company was based in Osby, Scania, in southern Sweden. It is best known for its wooden toy trains, sold in Europe since 1958. [edit&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Lekoseum")]. In 1984, the company started the BRIO Lekoseum (from Swedish "leka", to play), a toy museum featuring the company's products and those of other companies (such as Barbie dolls and Märklin model railways), at the headquarters in Osby. [edit&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Products")]. BRIO is best known for its wooden toy trains, sold in Europe since 1958. [edit&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Recent company history")]. In 2004, the Swedish investment company Proventus became the major shareholder of Brio with more than 40% of the votes. [edit&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: References")].

sources.title: Brio | Mental health for every child's flourishing
sources.snippet: Brio | Mental health for every child's flourishing. # Mental health for every child's flourishing. ## Starting in the classroom, with teachers who model what they teach. At Brio, we believe in the power of mental health skills to help children build lives of agency, joy, and purpose, even in tough circumstances. We work with teachers and public education leaders to make this possible for every child– equipping teachers first, so they live wellbeing before they teach it. From around age six, children spend much of their week in classrooms, often with a handful of teachers who can influence whether they feel safe and seen, and whether wellbeing is modelled, not just taught in theory. When teachers build mental health skills within themselves, their classrooms and communities can transform: children feel it, learn from it, and carry it forward. ## Children’s wellbeing in school begins with a teacher who embodies it.
